A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CONPAIR and EVOGEN. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and corresponding material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, generated-image comparisons and a human preference study, including Tables 3–5 and Figure 8.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds real-dataset training comparisons and human evaluations of the data-generation pipeline in Appendices A.5–A.6.

M1.justification: The contrastive image-generation pipeline, reverse alignment, three-stage curriculum, projection head and InfoNCE objective remain unchanged. Expanded caption-revision instructions in Appendix A.3 document the existing procedure; they do not establish a new algorithm or a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly evaluates training with COLA and BISON, adding retrieved real-image hard-negative data alongside synthetic CONPAIR. This substantially expands the training-data coverage examined. T2I-CompBench, Attend-and-Excite and Gen-AI evaluation coverage remains; Gen-AI moves to Appendix C.2 rather than disappearing.

E2.justification: V2 removes DALL-E 3 and SD3-Medium from the T2I-CompBench comparison in Table 3, although both remain in other comparisons. It also introduces COLA-trained and BISON-trained EVOGEN as alternative-data controls in Table 7. These changes materially alter the reported comparator coverage.

E3.justification: V2 adds matched-sample dataset comparisons and substantial human-evaluation protocols: 1,500 prompt-image pairs sampled proportionally across stages with five annotators per sample, plus 500 revised-caption examples divided among five annotators. Table 3 also drops the SD3-based EVOGEN configuration. Existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.5–A.6 add tests of alternative training datasets, question-set coverage, VQA accuracy across complexity stages and reverse-alignment caption quality. New examples illustrate generation failures and differences between real and synthetic contrastive pairs. The original dataset/loss/curriculum ablation is retained with unchanged results.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports three-run means and standard deviations for EVOGEN, such as color 71.04 with standard deviation 0.13. V1 reports only point estimates. This is a limited extension of uncertainty reporting to one result row, and does not establish that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results: Table 7 reports Complex scores of 33.15 for COLA training and 32.91 for BISON training versus 42.52 for CONPAIR; Table 8 reports VQA accuracies of 93.1%, 91.4% and 88.9% across stages. Appendix A.6 reports 94.6% preference for revised captions. Three Table 3 rows disappear, while retained benchmark means, Gen-AI results and original ablations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, contrastive loss and cosine-similarity definition in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The introduction withdraws the explicit claim to be the first work incorporating curriculum contrastive learning into diffusion models. The central contributions remain CONPAIR and the three-stage EVOGEN framework. The abstract foregrounds the curriculum rationale already present in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations that visual clutter in retrieved real-image pairs impedes learning specific compositional differences, and that category-focused instructions improve caption revision. It also explains why unusual object-attribute combinations are unsuitable for its data construction. These extend interpretation locally; the formal limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands documentation of prompt filtering, caption-revision instructions, human-study sampling and interfaces, and the existing manual filtering audit. Appendix C.1 identifies the category-specific T2I-CompBench scoring tools. The abstract changes access directions to a project page described as providing data, code and demos; the original numerical training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated related-work appendix covering multimodal models, image generation and LLM-based compositional approaches, including LayoutGPT. It also develops explicit positioning against COLA and BISON and withdraws the first-work novelty claim. This expands research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, makes local language and terminology edits, and changes the first author's displayed name. It moves the Gen-AI discussion into an expanded quantitative-results appendix and adds appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds figures illustrating a generation failure, caption revision, real-versus-synthetic pairs and two annotation interfaces, plus dataset-comparison and VQA-accuracy tables. Table 3 is restructured, and the Gen-AI table moves to the appendix. Figure 3 replaces one example pair; most existing plots and qualitative grids are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for CONPAIR through human checks of question coverage, VQA accuracy and caption revision, together with real-data training controls and limited uncertainty reporting. These address weaknesses in v1's reliance on automatic alignment scores. The benefit is moderated by removing DALL-E 3, SD3-Medium and EVOGEN-SD3 results from Table 3, which narrows the main benchmark evidence despite retaining Gen-AI results in the appendix.
